- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- When sentiment flips from bearish to bullish mid-period, model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend after a spike, true price often corrects; apply mean reversion by reducing forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overfit; reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- If sentiment is high and price is flat, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid “sentiment-driven inflation.”
